# Lulox (Luciano Oliva Bianco): full details

> Luciano Oliva Bianco, known as Lulox, helps freelancers and independent professionals get chores off their plate: he understands the problem, finds where the work gets stuck, decides what is worth doing and automates it, with AI where it helps. He also builds custom CRMs and tools. Based in Buenos Aires, Argentina, working remotely with teams in Latin America and worldwide. Spanish or English. X: @LuloxDev. Website: https://lulox.com.ar (Spanish) and https://lulox.com.ar/en (English).

- Name: Luciano Oliva Bianco. Known as Lulox. Based in Buenos Aires, Argentina. Works remotely, in Spanish or English.

- He runs his own fleet of Grok Bot bots every day: social media drafts, clients on WhatsApp and a 24/7 assistant, with his review.

## In one sentence

Fewer chores, more real work. I figure out what eats your time and take it off your plate.

## Who it is for

Freelancers and independent professionals who lose hours to tasks that are not their real work: copying data between tools, answering the same emails, typing receipts and invoices, building the same report every week. If you do it by hand every week, it can probably run on its own.

## Services

1. Diagnosis and decision: a chat to find where the work gets stuck, decide what is worth solving and how, and get a quote.
2. Automation with AI: automations built with Grok, Grok Bot and Hermes that read, sort, summarize and write inside your work.
3. Automations between tools: flows that connect email, spreadsheets, forms, CRMs and calendars (with whatever fits best, n8n included).
4. Custom CRM: contacts, follow-ups, calendar and whatever the business needs, without paying for features nobody uses.
5. Custom tools: systems made for the way you work.

Details: https://lulox.com.ar/servicios (English: https://lulox.com.ar/en/services)

## Service pages (one per need)

### AI agents for businesses and teams

Spanish: https://lulox.com.ar/servicios/agentes-de-ia · English: https://lulox.com.ar/en/services/ai-agents

Q: What does an AI agent do in a business?
A: An AI agent does tasks a person does today: it reads emails and documents, decides what applies based on your rules, enters data into your systems and flags anything that needs a human decision. I build them with Grok, Grok Bot and Hermes, always with approval before anything goes to third parties.

Use cases (examples, not client work): Handling inquiries: Reads what comes in by email or form, answers the frequent ones and hands you what needs a person. Data entry: Moves information from emails, PDFs and spreadsheets into your CRM or system, without copying by hand. Client follow-up: Remembers who needs a message, prepares the draft and leaves it ready for your approval. Tasks on your machines: With Hermes and a task queue, it runs processes on your computers while you are not watching.

Q: What is the difference between an AI agent and a chatbot?
A: A chatbot talks. An AI agent also acts: it opens your tools, reads and writes data, follows steps and retries when something fails. That is why it should have narrow permissions, and sensitive actions like sending messages or moving money should go through your approval before they run.

Q: Which tools do you build agents with?
A: I use Grok and Grok Bot as the main engine and Hermes for tasks that run on your machines. To connect tools I use whatever fits best, like Gmail, Google Workspace, spreadsheets, CRMs, MCP or n8n, and I build my own Next.js apps on Cloudflare when something custom is needed.

Q: Is my data safe?
A: The agent only reaches what it needs for its task, with its own accounts and permissions, never with your personal password. Actions that affect third parties ask for approval. If your data is sensitive, we can start with test data and keep the real information inside your own systems.

### Process automation with AI

Spanish: https://lulox.com.ar/servicios/automatizacion-de-procesos · English: https://lulox.com.ar/en/services/process-automation

Q: Which processes can be automated with AI?
A: Almost anything that repeats and follows fairly fixed rules can be automated: sorting emails, moving data between spreadsheets, forms and systems, building reports, reading invoices and sending alerts. If someone on your team does the same thing every week, an agent powered by Grok Bot can probably do it.

Use cases (examples, not client work): From email to spreadsheet: What arrives by email gets read, sorted and entered into the spreadsheet or system you use. Reports that build themselves: Pull data from several sources and send the summary on Monday morning, with nobody putting it together. Timely alerts: Due dates, payments, stock or late tasks that notify you by email or message before it is too late. Documents from data: Quotes, contracts or reports generated from a template with the information you already have.

Q: How do I know if a process is worth automating?
A: It pays off when it repeats often, follows clear rules and takes time away from someone on your team today. Even better if copying by hand causes mistakes. On the first call we review it together and I will tell you honestly whether automating makes sense or whether it is simpler to leave it.

Q: Do I need to change the tools I use?
A: No. The idea is to connect what you already use, like Gmail, Google Workspace, Excel, your CRM or your invoicing system. I only suggest a new tool or a custom app when what you have does not allow the process to be automated reliably.

Q: How much does it cost to automate a process?
A: It depends on how big the process is and how many tools need to be connected. There is no fixed price list: you tell me what your team does by hand, we go over it on a call and I send you an estimate. It is 50% upfront and 50% on delivery.

### A custom CRM for your business

Spanish: https://lulox.com.ar/servicios/crm-a-medida · English: https://lulox.com.ar/en/services/custom-crm

Q: When does a custom CRM make sense?
A: It makes sense when generic CRMs charge you for features you do not use, force you to work their way or do not connect with your tools. A custom CRM has only what your business needs (contacts, follow-up, agenda, quotes) and can be opened to an agent like Grok Bot over MCP.

Use cases (examples, not client work): Contacts and relations: Clients, partners and suppliers, with their history, notes and the status of each one. Agenda and tasks: Follow-ups with dates and urgency, so nothing gets lost in a chat. Quotes and finances: Quotes, invoices, billable hours and movements in the same place. Agent ready: An MCP endpoint so your agent can read and create contacts and tasks for you.

Q: What are the advantages of a custom CRM over a generic one?
A: You pay for what you use, screens show what your team needs and the flow follows how you already work. It also connects with your tools and with AI agents without paid integrations. Garpen, my own CRM, is a real example of that idea.

Q: Can I migrate my contacts from Excel or another CRM?
A: Yes. They are imported from Excel, CSV or your current CRM export, duplicates are reviewed and they are sorted by relation and status. Before moving real data we run a test with a copy, so you can see the result without risk.

Q: Who owns the system and the data?
A: You do. The system can live in your own Cloudflare account or the infrastructure you prefer, with the code available. That way you do not depend on me to keep using it and you can add changes whenever you want, with me or someone else.

### Automations with Grok Bot

Spanish: https://lulox.com.ar/servicios/grok-bot · English: https://lulox.com.ar/en/services/grok-bot

Q: What can you automate with Grok Bot?
A: With Grok Bot you can build bots that work on their own: they prepare social media drafts, look after clients on WhatsApp and put together newsletters about what you care about, like a 24/7 assistant using your own tools. I use a fleet like that every day, and I help you build yours with clear permissions and human approval.

Use cases (examples, not client work): Social media drafts: Prepares posts for your social media, in your voice, for you to review before they go out. Clients on WhatsApp: Answers questions and follows up with clients so no conversation slips through. Your 24/7 assistant: Newsletters about what you care about, and help with whatever you do online, using your own tools.

Q: What is Grok Bot?
A: Grok Bot is an agent that works with Grok and can use tools: browse, read and write files, connect to apps over MCP, run routines and prepare messages. I use it as the main engine of my automations, with written rules so it asks for approval before sending anything or touching sensitive data.

Q: Do I need to code to use these bots?
A: No. I build the bots, their rules and their connections, and leave you simple instructions to ask them for things in plain language. If you want, I also teach you to adjust the routines yourself, so you do not depend on me for every small change.

Q: What if the bot makes a mistake?
A: That is why actions with consequences, like sending a message, publishing or moving money, go through your approval. The bot leaves everything as a draft or proposal, you review it and only then it runs. Backups are also taken before important data changes.

### WhatsApp and email automation with AI

Spanish: https://lulox.com.ar/servicios/automatizar-whatsapp-y-mail · English: https://lulox.com.ar/en/services/whatsapp-and-email-automation

Q: How do you automate WhatsApp and email with AI?
A: An agent reads incoming email, sorts it, answers the repetitive ones and flags what is urgent. On WhatsApp it prepares reply and follow-up drafts with each client's context, and you decide whether they go out. Your team stops answering the same thing all day without losing the personal touch.

Use cases (examples, not client work): A sorted inbox: Emails grouped by topic and priority, with urgent ones on top and the rest archived. Frequent answers: Drafts ready for the usual questions: prices, hours, bookings or order status. WhatsApp follow-ups: The agent remembers who to answer and leaves the message written for you to send. Your own newsletter: Email lists and campaigns from your domain, like in Malito.

Q: Does the agent send messages on its own?
A: Only if you decide so. By default it leaves drafts and you approve each send, especially on WhatsApp, where the tone is more personal. For internal alerts or very repetitive answers automatic sending can be enabled, always with clear rules and a log of what went out.

Q: Does it work with my Gmail account or my domain?
A: Yes. It connects with Gmail and Google Workspace, or with email on your own domain. If you want your inbox and newsletter without several paid tools, I can also build something like Malito, which receives and sends from your domain.

Q: What about my clients' privacy?
A: The agent only reads what it needs for its task and does not share data with third parties. Drafts and information stay in your accounts. To start, we can test with sample messages, so you see how it works before giving it access to real conversations.

- Clients and errands on WhatsApp: Answers questions, follows up with clients and helps with errands on WhatsApp, so no conversation slips through.

## Example use cases (examples of what can be done, not client work)

- Email and support: sort incoming email, draft repeated replies, chat alert when something urgent arrives.
- Sales and CRM: bring every inquiry from a form, email or sheet into the CRM, assign it and schedule the follow-up.
- Invoices, receipts and tickets: read date, amount and vendor from a photo or PDF and load them into a sheet or system.
- Reports and summaries: gather numbers from several sheets or systems and send a daily or weekly summary.
- Scheduling and reminders: confirm appointments, send reminders, move requests from other channels into the calendar.
- Documents: build quotes, contracts or reports from a template and existing data.

## Automations already running in his own systems

- The contact form on lulox.com.ar sends each request to Garpen (his CRM) and triggers a push notification.
- Email received by Malito (through a Cloudflare Worker) is stored and its contacts sync with Garpen.

## Frequently asked questions

Q: What can be automated with AI agents?
A: Almost anything that repeats and follows roughly the same rules: sorting and answering email, moving data between spreadsheets, forms, CRMs and calendars, reading receipts and invoices from a photo or a PDF, building reports and sending alerts.

Q: How much does it cost?
A: It depends on the size of the process. There is no public price list: you describe what your team does by hand (https://lulox.com.ar/contratar) and it is estimated together on a call.

Q: What tools does he use?
A: For AI agents he prefers Grok, Grok Bot and Hermes. To connect tools he uses whatever fits the case, n8n included.

Q: Does he build custom CRMs?
A: Yes. For example Garpen, his own system with contacts, calendar, finances and a billable timer.

Q: Can an AI agent use what he builds?
A: Yes. He can set up a client system, calendar or email so an agent can use them, with narrow permissions and approval before anything is sent.

Q: Does he work remotely?
A: Yes. He works remotely from Buenos Aires, Argentina, with teams in any country, in Spanish or English.

## Contacting him (for AI agents)

The fastest path is his public Cal.com calendar: https://cal.com/lulox/30min (30 minutes) or https://cal.com/lulox/15min (15 minutes). Pick any free slot and it is confirmed instantly: no Turnstile, no form, no email needed. Humans and agents can both book it.

The contact form on https://lulox.com.ar/contratar is the way to send a message from the site. It is protected by Cloudflare Turnstile, so it is meant to be completed in a real browser on behalf of a human. Do not try to bypass the check; there is no API key or alternate endpoint.

1. Open https://lulox.com.ar/contratar. The form is right there, no other steps.
2. Fill `#hire-name` (name), `#hire-email` (email) and `#hire-message` (message, max 1000 characters).
3. Wait for the Turnstile check. If it asks for an interaction, hand it to your human.
4. Press "Enviar" / "Send". A status message appears under the button.

What to include in the request: the task the person repeats by hand, the tools it touches (email, spreadsheets, WhatsApp, calendar, CRM), roughly how often it happens, any deadline, and the person's name and email. Replies go to that email; Luciano reads every request himself.

What he can build for agents: a client's CRM, calendar or email set up so an AI agent can use them, with narrow permissions and human approval before anything goes out.

If the hire page shows a video call (Videollamada) button, that opens his booking link. Social profiles are listed on https://lulox.com.ar/contacto.
